summary: The tutor and student are discussing how to solve quadratic equations by factorisation, how roots relate to the graph crossing the x-axis, and when other methods like the quadratic formula become useful.

timeline.speaker: Tutor
timeline.text: Let's look at x squared plus five x plus six equals zero and see if we can factorise it.

timeline.speaker: Student
timeline.text: So I need two numbers that multiply to six and add to five.
timeline.summary: Student identifies the factor pair strategy.

timeline.speaker: Tutor
timeline.text: Exactly, and once we have the factors we can see the roots straight away.

timeline.speaker: Student
timeline.text: Are the roots the same as where the graph crosses the x-axis?
timeline.summary: Student connects algebra to graph interpretation.

timeline.speaker: Tutor
timeline.text: Yes, the roots are the x-intercepts, and if factorising is awkward we can switch to the quadratic formula.
timeline.summary: Tutor confirms graphical meaning and introduces an alternative method.

items.definition: A value of x that makes the quadratic equal zero.
Rewriting an expression as a product of brackets.

widgets.title: Worked Example
steps: Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5.

widgets.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using numbers that multiply correctly but do not add correctly.
Forgetting to set each bracket equal to zero.
Dropping the sign when writing the roots.
